AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.7.1 through 0.8.4, an incomplete IPv6 blocklist in AutoGPT's outbound SSRF protection allows authenticated users to reach local or private network services. Specifically, _is_ip_blocked and BLOCKED_IP_NETWORKS in autogpt_platform/backend/backend/util/request.py fail to reject the IPv6 unspecified address :: (which connects to ::1 on Linux) as well as 6to4, NAT64, Teredo, and deprecated IPv4-compatible IPv6 encodings. An attacker can pass :: directly to blocks/sql_query_block.py or blocks/email_block.py, or point URL-fetching blocks, web fetch, MCP servers, webhooks, or OAuth at a hostname whose AAAA record resolves to ::. On backends run directly on a host, this exposes unauthenticated internal RPC services and databases listening on ::1, though the default Docker Compose and single-container deployments bind internal services to IPv4 only. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0. 24/11/2026 24/11/2026 Vector CVSS:3.1 CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N Gravedad 3.1 (CVSS 3.1 Base Score) 7.70 Gravedad 3.1 Txt Gravedad 3.1 (CVSS 3.1 Base Score) HIGH
